function.name: calculate_projectile_range
function.description: Calculate the range of a projectile launched at an angle with initial velocity, using the kinematic equation. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

initial_velocity.description: The initial velocity at which projectile is launched. This is a float type value.

angle.description: The angle at which projectile is launched. This should be in degrees. This is a float type value.

time.description: The time in seconds after which the range is to be calculated. This is a float type value.

message.content:
The horizontal distance travelled by a projectile (or a “car” in this context) after a time \(t\) is simply the horizontal component of its initial velocity multiplied by that time:

\[
\text{distance} \;=\; v \,\cos(\theta)\; \times\; t
\]

where  

* \(v\) is the launch speed (m s⁻¹),  
* \(\theta\) is the launch angle measured from the horizontal (in radians or degrees – just be consistent),  
* \(t\) is the elapsed time (s).

If you want to compute this numerically using the provided function, you would call it like this (replace the placeholders with actual numbers):

```python
from functions import calculate_projectile_range

# Example values
initial_velocity = 20.0   # m/s
angle = 30.0              # degrees
time = 5.0                # seconds

result = calculate_projectile_range(
    initial_velocity=initial_velocity,
    angle=angle,
    time=time
)
print(result)
```

The function internally uses the same physics: it takes the horizontal component \(v \cos(\theta)\) and multiplies it by the specified time to give the range.
